Error.description: Any 4xx or 5xx: every error has this body. docs/api.md lists the codes with their statuses.

Forbidden.description: `insufficient_scope`, naming the scope in `scope`; `session_required`; or another refusal the operation has.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: the request needs an account and carries no valid token.

edits_sites.description: True for an account whoever runs the server named as one of Venti's partners for flying sites; left out for every other.

google_email.description: The email of the Google account the account is signed in to with, if it is linked to one. Only in the account's own answers.

AircraftKind.description: What kind of aircraft another network says a position is of. A word this version does not know is to be read as `unknown`.

name.description: What the pilot calls the alarm: 1 to 60 characters.

AlertRule.description: What an alarm waits for, told apart by `kind`: `wind`, `day` or `pilots`. A kind a client does not know is left as it is.

agree.description: true to agree, false to refuse.

Attribution.description: The credit of one data source an answer draws on. Whoever shows the data shows `text`, linked to `url`, next to it, and `notice` if there is one: the sources' licences require it. An answer's `attributions` has one entry per source it draws on, and only those.

redirect_to.description: The program's own address, as it registered it, with the code or the refusal, the program's state, and iss. The browser is sent there.

lasts.description: For how long the agreement holds, in the server's words.

may_not.description: What it may not do, in the server's words.

may_read.description: What the program may read once the pilot agrees, in the server's words: one sentence for each thing.

on_this_device.description: Whether that address is a program on the device the browser runs on.

program.description: What the program calls itself: its own claim, which nobody checked.

returns_to.description: The host the pilot's browser is sent back to with the answer.

Cable.description: One cable hung in the air, of exactly one source, as a line. A height is given only where the source maps one; no cable in an answer is no statement that there is none.

cheers.description: How many pilots cheer the flight now.

cheered.description: Whether the account that asks cheered the flight. Absent when nobody is signed in.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

text.description: Plain text of at most 500 characters. Show it as text, never as markup.
Plain text; at most 500 characters once trimmed.

count.description: How many comments the flight has now.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

open.description: False once the flight's pilot turned comments off; those written before stay.

ConfirmSiteRequest.description: "I took off here and it was good": the day, a line if wanted, and one of the pilot's own flights if wanted, by its address.

google_id_token.description: A fresh Google ID token of the linked Google account, in place of the password.
A fresh Google ID token of the linked Google account, in place of the password: what an account made with Google sends.

DumpContent.description: What a file of a dump holds: the sites of a layer as they stand, or every site the layer ever had with every revision.

DumpFile.description: One file of a layer's dump. `bytes` and `sha256` are of the file before any compression on the way.

DumpFormat.description: The format of a file of a dump: GeoJSON, CSV, or JSON Lines.

DumpLayer.description: The dump of one layer of Venti's own sites: the licence its records are given under, when its files were made, the layer's change number they stand at (`cursor`, to go on from with `GET /v1/sites/changes`), how much they hold, and the files.

ErrorBody.description: `code` is stable and for programs; `message` is for the person writing the client and may change. `scope` comes with `insufficient_scope`, `site` with `site_too_close`.

ErrorCode.description: A stable code. `x-venti-values` lists the codes the server has today; docs/api.md says which status each comes with and when. A client must expect codes it does not know.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every answer with a 4xx or 5xx status.

cheered.description: Whether the account that asks cheered the flight.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `before`. Absent on the last page.

cursor.description: Send it as `since` with the next request.

more.description: Whether more waits: ask again at once with `cursor`.

reset.description: True when the cursor sent was not this server's: what follows starts from the oldest kept.

FiredBecause.description: What fired an alarm, told apart by `kind`: a reading of the station, a run of the thermal map, or a count of the pilots in the air.

Flight.description: A flight as worked out by the server from the uploaded file. `id` is its address for good and is never used for another flight.

cursor.description: Send it as `since` with the next request.

more.description: Whether more changes wait: ask again at once with `cursor`.

reset.description: True when the cursor sent was not this server's: drop what you hold and keep what the answers from here on give.

FlightSite.description: The site a flight took off from: the standing take-off within 500 m of its take-off, a partner's before a place from pilots before a source's, and of one layer the nearest. Looked up with every answer.

FlightTerms.description: Under what terms the flights of an answer may be used by somebody other than their pilot. Read it from each answer and act on it as it stands that day. `decided: false` marks a holding statement: the terms are not settled, and `licence` is absent until they are.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

FlownThermalCell.description: A cell of the grid in which the public flights of at least `min_pilots` pilots climbed. No pilot, no flight, no day.

climb_ms.description: The climbs' average, m/s, to a tenth.

from_m.description: The height a climb began at, on average, rounded to 50 m.

to_m.description: The height a climb ended at, on average, rounded to 50 m.

FlownThermalsResponse.description: Where thermals have been: Venti's own, from the public flights the server holds, under their terms. The cells with the most pilots come first; the least number of pilots is counted after `month` and `hours` are applied.

flights.description: How many public flights the server has read for this.

hours.description: The hours asked for, by the sun at the place: from the first to before the second. Left out for the whole day.

month.description: The month asked for, 1 to 12; left out for the whole year.

followers.description: How many accounts follow the pilot now.
How many accounts follow the pilot, those the list does not name included.

following.description: How many accounts the pilot follows, those the list does not name included.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

you_follow.description: Whether the account that asks follows the pilot. Absent when nobody is signed in, and in the account's own list.

flights.description: How many public flights the pilot has.

GoogleSignInAnswer.description: 201 with SignInResponse for a Google account linked to an account; 200 with GoogleSignUpResponse for one that is not.

id_token.description: The ID token Google gave the app, for one of the server's client IDs.

GoogleSignUpResponse.description: A first sign-in with Google: the pilot chooses a handle and the app sends it with `signup` to POST /v1/auth/google/account.

signup.description: Good for a quarter of an hour, on this server only.

google_sign_in.description: Whether the server offers signing in with Google.

cursor.description: Send it as `since` with the next request.

more.description: Whether more changes wait: ask again at once with `cursor`.

reset.description: True when the cursor sent was not this server's: drop what you hold and keep what the answers from here on give.

LiveClimb.description: A place where paragliders or hang gliders circled and climbed in the last minutes. It names the air and no glider: `position` is the middle of a cell of the grid, and nothing says who climbed.

age_s.description: How long before `time` the last of them was last heard circling in it, seconds.

climb_ms.description: The climb averaged over the circles of every pilot who worked it, m/s, to a tenth.

from_m.description: The lowest height a pilot began to circle at, metres above sea level, rounded to 50 m.

pilots.description: How many pilots circled in it in the last `listed_minutes`.

to_m.description: The greatest height a pilot circled to, rounded to 50 m.

LiveClimbsLayer.description: The climbs one source of live positions shows: a network, whose credit is the attribution of the same source, or `venti`, Venti's own live pilots who show their flight to everyone.

LiveClimbsResponse.description: Where pilots climb now, in layers by where the positions come from; the layers are never one record. Derived by a fixed rule (circling and climbing) from the positions of the last minutes; nothing of a glider that must not be shown is in it.

cell_deg.description: The side of a cell of the grid a climb's place is the middle of, degrees.

LiveSitesLayer.description: The sites one source of live positions has pilots in the air at, the most pilots first. A site that is not listed has none.

LiveSitesResponse.description: How many pilots are in the air at the flying sites of a box, in layers by where the positions come from. A pilot whom a network hears and who sends Venti a live track is in both layers: they are not to be added up.

NotificationKind.description: What a pilot is told of. A client skips a kind it does not know.

cursor.description: Send it as `since` with the next request.

more.description: Whether more waits: ask again at once with `cursor`.

reset.description: True when the cursor sent was not this server's: what follows starts from the oldest kept.

takeoff_site.description: The name of the site the flight took off from, as it stood then.

OtherAircraft.description: An aircraft another network heard, where it was last heard. `id` stays the same while the server runs and is not the device's address. `registration`, `competition_id` and `model` are there only where the owner let the aircraft be identified.

next.description: The cursor of the next page: send it as `after`. Absent on the last page.

PilotSeason.description: A year by UTC of a pilot's public flights.

by_month.description: Flights by the month of the year they began in, January first: twelve numbers.

distance_m.description: The scoring distances of the flights that score, added up, in metres.

points.description: The sum of the points of the best `counted` flights, as a ranking of the same span gives it.

PilotsAlert.description: Pilots in the air at a place: fires when at least `min_pilots` paragliders and hang gliders are in the air within 5 km of it by one source of live positions, then rests `rest_hours` hours. The server looks once a minute.

cursor.description: Send it as `since` with the next request.

more.description: Whether more changes wait: ask again at once with `cursor`.

reset.description: True when the cursor sent was not this server's: drop what you hold and keep what the answers from here on give.

public_key.description: The server's P-256 public key, uncompressed, base64url without padding: the `applicationServerKey` of `pushManager.subscribe`.

auth.description: The browser's authentication secret, 16 bytes, base64url.

p256dh.description: The browser's P-256 public key, uncompressed, base64url.

PushSubscriptionRequest.description: A browser's `PushSubscription`, as its `toJSON()` gives it.

endpoint.description: The address of the push service the browser was given: HTTPS, of a push service the server sends to, at most 1024 bytes.

month.description: The month by UTC, written YYYY-MM, as the ranking's `month` takes it.

from.description: The first moment of the span the ranking counts, as `from` or `month` asked for it. Left out for a ranking of all time.

month.description: The month the ranking is of, written YYYY-MM, when `month` asked for one.

to.description: The first moment after that span. Left out when it has no end.

RankingYear.description: A year in which a public flight that scores started, with its months that have one, the newest first.

Scope.description: What a token for another program may do. `x-venti-values` lists the scopes there are today.

Site.description: A flying site, of exactly one source or of one of Venti's own two layers. Records of two sources are never merged.

SiteAir.description: A flying site and the pilots in the air around it: two numbers and the site's identifier, as `GET /v1/sites` names it.

airborne.description: Paragliders and hang gliders in the air within `within_m` of the site, heard in the last five minutes.

took_off.description: Those that took off there in the last `took_off_minutes`.

SiteBestFlight.description: One of a site's best public flights: what names it. The rest of it is at `GET /v1/flights/{id}`.

SiteCandidate.description: A place where the public flights of several pilots began and no site stands. It names no pilot and no flight; its position is the middle of the take-offs rounded to 0.0001 degrees, its height their mean rounded to 10 m.

altitude_m.description: Satellite altitude, metres above mean sea level.

by_month.description: Twelve numbers, January first: how many of the flights began in each month of the year, all years together.

SiteCandidatesResponse.description: The places in a box where pilots take off and no site of any layer stands: something to show a pilot who flew there, who may add the site. The server makes no site of a candidate. The one with the most pilots comes first; `more` says that the box holds more than are listed.

cell_deg.description: The side of the cell of the grid in which a candidate's flights began, degrees of latitude and of longitude.

clear_of_sites_m.description: How far from a candidate no site stands, metres.

min_pilots.description: The least number of different pilots whose public flights began at a candidate.

cursor.description: Send it as `since` with the next request.

more.description: Whether more changes wait: ask again at once with `cursor`.

removals.description: The same sites in the same order, each with its name, who removed it and when.

removed.description: The sites that are gone, by identifier: all a mirror needs to remove them.

reset.description: True when the cursor sent was not this server's: drop what you hold and keep what the answers from here on give.

SiteConfirmation.description: One pilot's confirmation of a site. `with_flight` is there, and true, where the server found a flight of the pilot's that took off at the site.

SiteConfirmationsResponse.description: Who says they took off at a site: at most the newest 100.

SiteConfirmed.description: How many pilots say they took off at a site and that it was good, and the newest day one of them speaks of. Left out of a site's `standing` while nobody has.

SiteFlightsResponse.description: What the public flights that began within `within_m` metres of a site say about it. Made anew for every answer from flights their pilots made public and from nothing else: a flight that is private, shared by link, taken down or deleted is in no count. A day is the day at the site, by the sun.

best.description: The best of them by points, the best first: at most five. A flight too short to score is not among them.

by_month.description: Twelve numbers, January first: how many of the flights began in each month of the year, all years together.

latest_day.description: The day of the newest of the flights. Absent without a flight.

takeoff.description: Whether the site is one to take off from by its own record: `takeoff` or `towing` among its uses, or no use named. For one that is not, nothing is counted: every count is 0 and `best` is empty.

within_m.description: How far from the site's position a flight may have taken off to be counted, metres.

SiteRemoval.description: A site that is gone, as a list of removed sites names it. `name` is as the site last stood, and absent for a site that whoever runs the server took down. `by` is absent where whoever runs the server removed it and where the account is gone.

TokenClient.description: On a token that came of the pilot's agreement on the server's own page with a program that asked there: the program, and the one address the token is good at. Left out on a token the pilot made by hand.

Visibility.description: Who may read a flight: `private` its pilot, `unlisted` whoever has its address, `public` everyone, in the lists too.

session.description: The token of a sign-in (`POST /v1/sessions`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer …`. It may do everything the account may. The server sets no cookies and reads none.

token.description: A token a pilot made for another program (`POST /v1/account/tokens`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer venti_pat_…`. It may do what its scopes say; an operation names the scope it needs.

info.description:
Made by the server from its own table of routes and held to it by tests. docs/api.md in the repository says in words what every field means, when each error comes and what the bounds are; `x-venti-docs` on an operation names its heading there, and "Writing a program against Venti" is where to begin.

Within `/v1` the format only grows: an answer may gain fields and a list of known values may gain entries, so a client ignores what it does not know. No schema here closes a record against further fields. Where a schema has `x-venti-values`, those are the values there are today, and others may come.

A value that is not known is left out of an answer: a field is never null. Null stands only inside a list with an entry per cell of the thermal map's grid, for a cell without a value; its schema says so.

The data of others is handed out under its sources' licences: every answer that carries such data names them in `attributions`, and answers with flights of pilots carry `terms`.
